title: Astrid and the Inheritance
premise: Astrid Vane, the night concierge of the Marlowe Grand Hotel, has spent fifteen years quietly recording every guest, lie, and disappearance in her private ledgers. When town founder Jonah Thackeray is exhumed for a land dispute and his coffin proves empty, investigators discover Astrid's files contain details about his death that only a witness—or a killer—could know. As suspicion falls on her, Astrid realizes the empty coffin was staged to flush out someone who has been hiding in plain sight for fifteen years: the person who helped Thackeray fake his death, then murdered him for real. To clear her name she must reconstruct that final night from memory, ledgers, and a guest who never checked out—and trap the killer before they destroy the last ledger, and Astrid with it.
about_author: Jude Eastwick is a former hotel auditor who spent a decade working graveyard shifts in small-town hospitality, where she learned that front desks see everything and forget nothing. She writes mysteries about ordinary people whose meticulous habits make them dangerous witnesses.

chapters.title: The Night Register
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Establishes her ritual: logging arrivals, departures, and oddities at the Marlowe Grand's desk. A lawyer arrives asking strange questions about the hotel's founding era. Emotional beat: the comfort of order, faintly disturbed by the sense that something old is stirring.

chapters.title: Exhumation Day
chapters.summary: Astrid watches from the hotel steps as workers open founder Jonah Thackeray's monument vault across the square. The crowd goes silent; police tape blooms. She recognizes the lawyer among them, pale. Emotional beat: dread—the past surfacing like a body.

chapters.title: Empty
chapters.summary: Detective Imogen Reyes interviews Astrid because the hotel overlooks the cemetery. The coffin held sandbags and a 2009 newspaper. Astrid mentions, too casually, that she remembers the week Thackeray 'died.' Reyes's eyes sharpen. Emotional beat: Astrid realizes her memory is now evidence.

chapters.title: The Ledgers
chapters.summary: Astrid retrieves her private notebooks—fifteen years of observations—from a locked drawer. Rereading October 2009, she finds gaps: three nights missing pages, torn out cleanly. Someone has been in her room. Emotional beat: violation; the archivist discovers her archive can be edited.

chapters.title: Guest Who Never Left
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, mixed with ledger excerpts. Room 412 has been paid annually by a shell company since 2010, occupied one week each October, always vacant when she checks. This year's booking is next week. Emotional beat: hunter's instinct awakening beneath fear.

chapters.title: The Widow's Account
chapters.summary: Astrid visits Thackeray's elderly widow, Eleanor, who insists she saw her husband alive three days after the funeral—in the hotel lobby. Astrid checks: no entry logged, but the lobby camera disc existed once. Emotional beat: grief weaponized; two keepers of memory aligning.

chapters.title: Person of Interest
chapters.summary: Reyes reveals the torn pages match paper found in Thackeray's original case file—someone inside the investigation fifteen years ago had access to Astrid's notes. Suspicion pivots to the retired lead detective, Harlan Croft. Emotional beat: paranoia; the file itself is untrustworthy.

chapters.title: Croft's Confession, Almost
chapters.summary: Astrid confronts Croft at his bait shop. He admits he closed the case fast—for money or fear he won't say—but swears the empty coffin isn't his work. He hands her an old key: Thackeray's, mailed to him anonymously last month. Emotional beat: uneasy alliance of guilty men and careful women.

chapters.title: Room 412
chapters.summary: Astrid picks the annual week early and enters 412: dust, a typewriter, and photographs of herself at the desk across fifteen years. She was being studied as long as she was studying others. Emotional beat: cold horror of reversed surveillance.

chapters.title: The Lawyer Returns
chapters.summary: The lawyer, Dana Okafor, reveals she represents Thackeray's estranged daughter, who commissioned the exhumation after receiving anonymous letters claiming her father lived until 2011. One letter enclosed a page from Astrid's own ledger. Emotional beat: betrayal—her private words used as ammunition.

chapters.title: October 2009, Reconstructed
chapters.summary: Interleaved flashback chapter: young Astrid's memories of the funeral week—a hooded figure carrying a heavy duffel through the service corridor at 3 a.m., the smell of lime, Thackeray's car moved. Emotional beat: memory returning like tide over buried things.

chapters.title: Sandbags
chapters.summary: Reyes confirms the coffin was filled recently—sand matching the hotel's renovation bags from 2022. The exhumation was staged from inside the Marlowe. Astrid realizes the killer wanted the grave opened, wanted the letters sent, wanted her implicated. Emotional beat: the trap snapping shut around her.

chapters.title: Arrest
chapters.summary: Astrid is detained when a ledger page placing her near the cemetery on the relevant night surfaces—forged in her handwriting style. In holding, she notices the interrogator quotes a detail that appears in no official file. Emotional beat: claustrophobia; justice inside the law failing her.

chapters.title: The Man in the Vent
chapters.summary: Released on a technicality arranged by Okafor, Astrid reviews maintenance logs: someone with a master key accessed the attic above the lobby monthly for years. The watcher lives in the building. Emotional beat: the hotel itself becomes a suspect.

chapters.title: Eleanor's Second Story
chapters.summary: Eleanor confesses: Jonah faked his death to escape creditors and blackmailers, and she helped—until he came back in 2011 wanting his life restored, and they fought. She saw who left with him that night but was paid to forget. Emotional beat: complicity and the price of silence.

chapters.title: The Name Behind the Desk
chapters.summary: Cross-referencing payroll, keys, and the 2011 fight date, Astrid identifies the long-term 'maintenance contractor' hired weeks after the funeral: Gerald Moss, the beloved retired porter everyone trusts, who trained Astrid herself. Emotional beat: heartbreak—the mentor as monster.

chapters.title: What Moss Knew
chapters.summary: Astrid finds Moss's motive: Thackeray's faked death had framed Moss's brother, who died in prison. Moss didn't kill Jonah out of malice—he killed him when Jonah refused to recant and clear the brother's name. Emotional beat: sympathy entangled with horror; justice outside the law curdling into murder.

chapters.title: Bait
chapters.summary: Astrid plants word that the final missing ledger pages—recording the 2011 night—are hidden in the hotel safe, and lets Moss see her alone at the night desk. Reyes stakes out the building. Emotional beat: terrified resolve; the noticer making herself the noticed.

chapters.title: The Long Shift
chapters.summary: Climax begins. Moss comes down at 3 a.m.—the same hour as 2009—and they speak across the desk like any guest and concierge while Reyes closes in. He disables the cameras; the power dies. Emotional beat: terrible intimacy between two people who have watched each other for years.

chapters.title: Ledger and Knife
chapters.summary: In the dark lobby, Moss forces Astrid to the safe; she stalls by reading aloud his brother's file, breaking his certainty. Reyes, guided by Astrid's earlier planted clues, takes him down as he lunges. Emotional beat: words as weapons; memory defeating violence.

chapters.title: What the Coffin Was For
chapters.summary: Resolution of the mystery: Moss staged the exhumation to force the county to declare Thackeray legally dead again and reopen his brother's case, using Astrid's ledgers as scapegoat evidence. The truth clears the brother posthumously anyway. Emotional beat: bitter vindication—justice achieved by crime's own design.

chapters.title: New Register
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Astrid reopens the desk, starts a fresh ledger, and gives Eleanor the dignity of a true account of Jonah's end. Reyes leaves a card: consult, not suspect. Final image: Astrid writes the first line of a new page. Emotional beat: quiet restoration—memory kept honestly this time.
